metadata.title: Prime Numbers Without Trial-and-Error Overkill
metadata.description: Master primality tests, factor-pair reasoning, prime residues, and structured prime sequences.

content.text: A prime has exactly two positive factors. To test a candidate n, you only need to check prime divisors up to √n. This cuts the work dramatically.

For primes above 3, the number must be 1 or 5 modulo 6. Factor-pair overlap is also powerful: if two products share the middle primes, the ordered prime sequence can often be reconstructed immediately.
Start with the definition of a prime.
Prime questions often hide a parity shortcut. A sum of three odd primes is odd, so an even total forces the presence of the only even prime, 2.
Now use the mod-6 prime shortcut.
Use overlapping prime products to reconstruct an ordered set.
Great. Your prime toolkit now includes square-root testing, residue shortcuts, and factor structure.
